name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.4.0 — scheduled mutation replay: new /spec:replay + replay.js harness inject one hand-authored corpus-class defect (spec/doctrine/replay-corpus.md, 6 classes) into a just-CLEANed spec's tree in a marker-guarded scratch worktree and dispatch the standard reviewer blind to it; catch/miss/leg-caught lands as a `stage:"replay"` ledger row plus a retained evidence artifact, and `replay.js --stats` derives the catch-rate; /spec:review's CLEAN close now warns when a replay is due (every 5th review, at minimum once per major version); core.md § Feedback Loop names the cadence policy and rules a sustained miss-rate as the evidence that reopens the second-reviewer question. 7.3.0 — review evidence retention: verdict.js gains a required `--retain <dir>` on authoritative review-profile rows, writing `.claude/spec-runs/<runId>.json` (manifest legs untruncated, reviewer survivors/killed verbatim) that rides the close commit past the Phase 3 hygiene sweep; /spec:escape derives `killedMatch` from that artifact instead of user memory, falling back to memory only when none exists; /spec:plan's lock now appends a `stage:"plan"` ledger row of executed facts before the status flip; core.md § Feedback Loop names the escape ledger and reviewer replay catch-rate as the pipeline's only two ground-truth signals, self-reported review quality explicitly subordinate to both. 7.2.0 — ledger truth: verdict.js counts findings-leg findings (parsed, floored at 1 per red row) into the undispositioned pool so CLEAN is unreachable while a red leg sits undispositioned, and the disposition-contradiction guard widens to match; ledger leg rows retain their `observed` string in both profiles; review ledger rows always carry a generated-or-passed `runId`; build.md's `deviations`/`diff.loc` ledger definitions corrected to match what verdict.js and review actually count.
